_note: Informal French, verlan and swear words in France (/savoirs/argot). Own draft, idioms-mistakes run (2026-11-11), not yet reviewed by a native teacher. reg: umgang (informal) | slang | vulgaer (rude); stufe (vulgaer only): 1 mild, 2 strong, 3 very strong. w, bsp and the hoeflich pairs are French; std is the standard word with its English meaning; info is English. variety on every entry, frCA only where Québec usage differs, regional for Belgium/Switzerland. No slurs and no insults about groups of people (content-plan §5.7).

stufen.name: Standard French
stufen.wo: offices, work, exams, letters, the préfecture
stufen.satz: Pourriez-vous m'accorder un instant, s'il vous plaît ?

gruppen.titel: Short forms: how people really speak
gruppen.intro: Spoken French drops sounds and small words: ne disappears, on replaces nous, tu and je shrink. Don't write these forms in a letter or an exam, but you will hear them every day.

eintraege.std: Je ne comprends pas. (I don't understand.)
eintraege.bsp: Désolé, je comprends pas : vous pouvez répéter ?
eintraege.info: The ne of the negation is almost never said in speech. In writing and in exams it stays: ne … pas. Listen for pas alone.

eintraege.std: Je ne sais pas. (I don't know.)
eintraege.bsp: J'sais pas, demande à Karim.
eintraege.info: Je ne sais pas becomes “chais pas” or “j'sais pas”. You will hear it every day: you do not have to say it.

eintraege.std: Tu as une minute ? (Have you got a minute?)
eintraege.bsp: T'as une minute ? J'ai une question sur le contrat.
eintraege.info: tu + vowel often loses its u: t'as, t'es, t'inquiète. Fine among colleagues you say tu to. With vous there is no such short form.

eintraege.std: Nous y allons ? / Allons-y ? (Shall we go?)
eintraege.bsp: On mange à midi ? – Oui, on y va !
eintraege.info: In speech on replaces nous almost always. The verb is the il form: on va, on a, on est. In writing for exams, nous is safer; on is correct and common in letters between friends.

frCA.note: Same in Québec; there on also replaces nous in everyday speech.

eintraege.std: Il n'y a pas de souci. (No problem.)
eintraege.bsp: Y a du pain ? – Non, y en a plus.
eintraege.info: Il y a is pronounced “ya”, often “y a” in writing. Il n'y a pas → “y a pas”. “Y a plus” = il n'y en a plus.

eintraege.bsp: J'suis crevé, j'vais me coucher.
eintraege.info: Je is swallowed in front of a consonant: j'suis, j'vais, j'peux. Never write it in a formal text.

frCA.note: In Québec je suis often sounds like “chu” or “chus”, and je vais like “chu” or “j'vas”.

eintraege.std: Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? / Que fais-tu ? (What are you doing?)
eintraege.bsp: Tu fais quoi ce week-end ?
eintraege.info: Questions in speech: raising your voice at the end, or the question word at the end (tu vas où ?). Est-ce que and inversion are for careful speech and writing.

frCA.note: In Québec questions often end with -tu: “Tu viens-tu ?”, “C'est-tu prêt ?”.

eintraege.bsp: C'est quoi, ce papier ? Je dois le signer ?
eintraege.info: Quoi after a verb is the spoken question: C'est quoi ? Il veut quoi ? In writing: Qu'est-ce que c'est ?

eintraege.std: Il faut y aller. (We have to go.)
eintraege.bsp: Faut y aller, sinon on rate le train.
eintraege.info: The il of il faut is dropped in speech: faut, and also faudra, fallait.

eintraege.bsp: Ouais, ça marche, à tout à l'heure !
eintraege.info: Very common among friends. With a client, in an interview or at an office desk: oui. Also “ouais, bof” = so-so.

eintraege.bsp: T'inquiète, je m'en occupe.
eintraege.info: Another dropped ne: t'inquiète, t'occupe. Only to people you tutoie.

eintraege.std: Je ne sais pas, peut-être. (I don't know, maybe.)
eintraege.bsp: P't-être qu'il viendra, p't-être pas.
eintraege.info: Peut-être is often “p't-être” or “ptêt”. It is spoken only.

gruppen.intro: Words your colleagues, neighbours and friends use all the time. Informal, but not rude: you can say most of them to people you tutoie.

eintraege.bsp: Je rentre du boulot vers dix-huit heures.
eintraege.info: Very common. In a job interview or a CV: travail, emploi, poste. “Un petit boulot” = a part-time or odd job.

frCA.note: In Québec job (une job) is the everyday word; boulot is understood.

eintraege.bsp: Elle bosse dans un hôpital à Lyon.
eintraege.info: Informal verb, regular -er. “Bosser” also means to study hard: “Il a bossé pour l'examen.”

eintraege.bsp: J'ai acheté un bouquin sur l'histoire de Paris.
eintraege.info: A friendly word for a book. In class and in writing: livre.

eintraege.bsp: Ma bagnole est au garage depuis lundi.
eintraege.info: Informal. Neutral: voiture, véhicule (also on a form).

frCA.note: In Québec the usual word is un char (une auto); bagnole is understood.

eintraege.bsp: C'est quoi, ce truc ? – Aucune idée, un machin pour la cuisine.
eintraege.info: Truc is the all-purpose word when you don't know or don't want to name something. “Avoir le truc” = to know the trick.

eintraege.std: un homme, une femme (a guy, a girl)
eintraege.bsp: Un mec m'a demandé l'heure dans le métro.
eintraege.info: Informal, not an insult. “Nana” is more dated and can sound slightly macho: prefer “une femme” or “une fille” with people you don't know.

frCA.note: In Québec un gars (a guy) and une fille; “ma blonde / mon chum” = girlfriend / boyfriend.

eintraege.bsp: Je pars en week-end avec des potes.
eintraege.info: Informal and friendly. “Mon ami” is the neutral word.

eintraege.bsp: Ton voisin est très sympa : il m'a aidé à déménager.
eintraege.info: Short for sympathique. Invariable in the plural: des gens sympas (the spelling sympas is correct and common), and the feminine stays sympa.

eintraege.w: un appart, un resto, un ordi
eintraege.std: un appartement, un restaurant, un ordinateur (a flat, a restaurant, a computer)
eintraege.bsp: On a trouvé un petit appart près du métro.
eintraege.info: French cuts long words: le prof, le ciné, le petit déj', l'apéro. These are in everyday use, but write the full word in formal text.

frCA.note: In Québec petit déjeuner is déjeuner, and déjeuner is dîner; dîner (evening) is souper.

eintraege.bsp: La bouffe de la cantine n'est pas terrible.
eintraege.info: Informal and a bit rough. Fine among friends, not at a dinner with your boss.

eintraege.std: aimer beaucoup (to love, to be into)
eintraege.bsp: Je kiffe cette chanson.
eintraege.info: Slang from Arabic, now used by everyone in France under about 50. For adults in formal settings: aimer, adorer.

eintraege.bsp: On galère pour trouver un logement à Paris.
eintraege.info: A very useful verb: galérer. The noun is la galère: “C'est la galère !” = it's a nightmare.

gruppen.intro: In class you learn argent and euros. You will still hear these a lot: you need to understand them, but you don't have to say them.

eintraege.w: le fric, la thune, le pognon
eintraege.bsp: Je n'ai plus de thune ce mois-ci.
eintraege.info: Three common slang words for money. Not for a bank or an office. “Avoir du fric” = to be rich.

eintraege.bsp: Ça coûte combien ? J'ai pas beaucoup de sous.
eintraege.info: Friendly, softer than fric. “Être sans le sou” is neutral.

eintraege.bsp: Ce sandwich m'a coûté dix balles !
eintraege.info: Balle = euro (formerly franc). Prices up to a few hundred euros, among friends. “Un billet de cent balles.”

eintraege.std: pas d'argent du tout (not a penny)
eintraege.bsp: Je n'ai pas un rond avant le 1er du mois.
eintraege.info: Rond = coin. An informal way to say you are broke.

eintraege.bsp: Je suis fauché en fin de mois.
eintraege.info: Used for yourself and for friends. Also “être à sec”.

eintraege.bsp: On a dû casquer deux mille euros pour les travaux.
eintraege.info: Both mean to pay, mostly a large or unwelcome sum.

eintraege.std: c'est très bon marché (it's dirt cheap)
eintraege.bsp: Ce manteau à vingt euros ? C'est donné !
eintraege.info: A good thing for the buyer. “C'est du vol !” = it's a rip-off.

eintraege.bsp: Il est radin : il ne laisse jamais de pourboire.
eintraege.info: An informal, rather negative word for someone who hates spending.

eintraege.bsp: Ça coûte nonante francs.
eintraege.info: In France you must say soixante-dix and quatre-vingt-dix. Septante and nonante are standard in Belgium and Switzerland (and huitante or octante in parts of Switzerland): you will hear them there and from people who live there.
eintraege.regional: Belgium and Switzerland say septante and nonante; Switzerland also huitante or octante.

gruppen.titel: Slang, verlan and young people's words
gruppen.intro: Verlan turns a word around (l'envers → verlan): femme → meuf, lourd → relou, fou → ouf. It started in the suburbs of Paris and is now general among young people. Listen for it, use it carefully.

eintraege.bsp: Cette meuf est drôle !
eintraege.info: Verlan: meuf is femme said backwards. It is slang among young people. Not formal. Some find it too casual: don't use it about someone you don't know.

eintraege.bsp: Ce voisin est relou : il fait du bruit tous les soirs.
eintraege.info: Verlan of lourd. “C'est relou” = it's annoying. Informal, friends only.

eintraege.bsp: Le concert était ouf !
eintraege.info: Verlan of fou. It can be good or bad: “un truc de ouf” = something unbelievable.

eintraege.bsp: Il y a un type chelou devant la porte.
eintraege.info: Verlan of louche. Slang, spoken.

eintraege.bsp: On fait une teuf samedi chez moi.
eintraege.info: Verlan of fête. Friends only. For a polite invitation: une soirée, une fête.

eintraege.bsp: Les keufs ont fermé la rue.
eintraege.info: Verlan of flic. Slang; flic itself is informal, and with an officer you say monsieur l'agent. Better not to say any of these to the police.

eintraege.bsp: Je kiffe ce film.
eintraege.info: Slang from Arabic, in everyday use among younger people.

eintraege.bsp: Ce resto est trop bien !
eintraege.info: Trop is “too”, but in slang it just means “very”: trop bon, trop cool. In careful French, trop = too much.

eintraege.bsp: Je suis grave fatigué.
eintraege.info: “Grave” used as an adverb: “Ça m'a grave plu.” Informal, younger speakers.

frCA.note: Also common in Québec among young people.

eintraege.bsp: Dix heures de queue pour un titre de séjour, c'est dingue.
eintraege.info: Informal reaction: dingue = crazy. Listen for the tone: it can be admiration or anger.

gruppen.intro: Swearing is everywhere in French films and on the street, so you need to recognise it. As a learner, a foreigner and an adult you will do better with the mild forms. Strength: 1 mild, 2 strong, 3 very strong.

eintraege.bsp: Zut, j'ai oublié mon passeport !
eintraege.info: A very mild way to react to bad luck. Fine in every situation, also with children and at work.

eintraege.bsp: Mince, le bus vient de partir !
eintraege.info: The polite form of merde. Fine almost anywhere. Similar: flûte, purée, punaise.

eintraege.bsp: Purée, il est déjà minuit !
eintraege.info: A soft exclamation, used in the whole country: for surprise or annoyance.

eintraege.bsp: Merde, j'ai raté mon train !
eintraege.info: Very common. Rude with strangers and at work, but not a big scandal among friends. “Merde” is also said to wish an actor luck, as in a theatre.

eintraege.bsp: Putain, il fait froid !
eintraege.info: Extremely frequent in speech, especially in the south of France, and often only a filler. It still is a strong swear word: do not use it with strangers, at work or with older people.

frCA.note: Québec swearing uses religious words (sacres) such as tabarnak. They are strong too: don't copy them.

eintraege.std: Je m'en fiche. / Cela m'est égal. (I don't care.)
eintraege.bsp: Je m'en fous, fais ce que tu veux.
eintraege.info: Rude, not very strong. Use je m'en fiche or ça m'est égal with others.

eintraege.bsp: Ferme-la, je veux dormir !
eintraege.info: Rude. Ta gueule is even stronger. Never say it to someone you don't know well.

eintraege.bsp: Casse-toi, je ne veux plus te voir.
eintraege.info: Rude and aggressive. Politer: laissez-moi, s'il vous plaît.

eintraege.bsp: Ce logiciel, c'est de la merde.
eintraege.info: Very common among friends. Never in a written complaint or to a customer.

eintraege.bsp: Ça me fait chier de refaire tous ces papiers.
eintraege.info: Vulgar, but very frequent. Everyone understands it; use ça m'énerve or ça m'agace instead.

eintraege.bsp: Bordel, où sont mes clés ?
eintraege.info: Strong. “Un bordel” also means a mess: “Quel bordel !”. Not for polite company.

eintraege.bsp: Ne sois pas con, appelle-la.
eintraege.info: Very common but an insult when said to a person. Among close friends “c'est con” just means “it's a pity”. Not with strangers or colleagues.

hoeflich.zu: Pourriez-vous parler moins fort, s'il vous plaît ?
